This looks like a real long-running memory growth issue rather than a single one-off allocation.

The most likely root causes are:

1. **Unbounded SSE/event buffering for long-lived windows**
   - The app keeps long-lived event streams open.
   - If a client/window becomes slow or disconnect cleanup does not happen promptly, queued events can keep accumulating in memory.
   - This is especially bad for high-frequency events (message deltas, tool updates, etc.), and is much more likely to produce multi-GB growth than heartbeats alone.

2. **Shell/tool output retained in memory**
   - Large stdout/stderr from bash/tool execution was being accumulated in memory instead of being capped/spilled early.
   - In a long-running session, a few large commands or repeated tool usage can compound badly.

3. **Session prompt subprocess output also had the same accumulation pattern**
   - There was a second output-retention path in prompt/session execution, so the problem was not limited to one tool path.

Why this matches the symptom: if one OpenCode window owns those queues/buffers, closing that single window would immediately release a very large amount of memory, which is exactly what was reported here.

So the short version is: **likely a combination of unbounded event queue growth + unbounded shell output retention over time**.

## Additional evidence: 1,500+ skills exhaust the entire context window

Adding data from my environment that shows this issue at scale.

### Environment
- OpenCode with `opencode-skills-antigravity` plugin (~1,330 skills) + LabClaw (~240 nested skills)
- NadirClaw proxy routing to AWS Bedrock (eu-west-2)
- Models: Kimi K2.5, Qwen3 480B, Qwen3 30B (all 262K token context)
- LiteLLM 1.83.0

### Measurements from NadirClaw raw request logs

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| `system_prompt_length` | 595,269 chars (595KB) |
| Skill `<skill>` XML blocks | 1,539 |
| Skill descriptions payload | ~580KB |
| OpenCode own instructions | ~9KB |
| User CLAUDE.md | ~5KB |
| Approximate tokens | ~148,817 |
| % of 262K context window | **56%** |

### Impact

- Every Bedrock model returns `BadRequestError` — even simple prompts like "hi" fail on `auto` mode
- All models in the fallback chain exhausted on multi-turn conversations with tool results
- Users see: "All configured models are currently unavailable"
- The 56% context consumption leaves insufficient room for conversation + tool results, so even models that accept the initial request fail on turn 2-3

### Workaround

Moved all skills from `~/.config/opencode/skills/` to a separate directory and use `@zenobius/opencode-skillful` plugin for lazy discovery. System prompt dropped from ~595KB to ~9KB.

This confirms the same root cause identified in this issue — skill descriptions should not be statically inlined into the system prompt.

Two biggest mouse-related issues I’ve run into:

Focus click selecting first option
When switching from another application back to OpenCode, clicking anywhere in the window immediately selects the first option.
This is quite disruptive — the first click should only restore focus, not trigger a selection.

Mouse mode persists after terminal crash
If the terminal crashes, mouse mode can remain active. Moving the mouse then prints raw escape codes to the screen - like a beautiful piece of 90's ASCII art.
(Workaround: running reset fixes it.)
Suggestion: More granular mouse configuration

Granular mouse control
It would be great to have fine-grained control over mouse behavior. Ideally, each interaction could be toggled via flags in the opencode config file:

- Enable/disable text selection via mouse drag
- Enable/disable auto-copy on selection release
- Enable/disable mouse-based option selection
- Keyboard-only mode (completely disable mouse interaction)
- Someone mentioned triple clicking for copying lines

This would allow users to tailor behavior to their workflow and avoid unintended input issues.

I'm experiencing a regression between opencode-ai@1.3.12 and newer builds (1.3.13+) that appears to be specific to third-party model providers.

Repro matrix

→ ✅ works with all providers
→ ❌ tool-call errors with third-party providers
→ ✅ works with official providers (DeepSeek, etc.)
Specific findings

Third-party provider failure: Using WuWenXinQiong API (providing access to GLM-5, Qwen, etc.) results in tool-call failures
Official provider success: Using DeepSeek official provider works perfectly
Error pattern: - empty tool name injected between normal tool calls
Multiple models affected: GLM-5, Qwen, and other models via WuWenXinQiong API all fail
Same model works elsewhere: GLM-5 via official Kimi provider also fails (as reported in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20577)
Symptoms

Tool calls get aborted with "Tool execution aborted"
Invalid empty tool injected between normal tool calls
All tool functionality broken when using third-party providers
No issues when switching to official DeepSeek provider
Why this looks like a provider-handling regression

Same model architecture (GLM-5) fails via third-party but works via official provider
Regression is strictly version-bound (1.3.12 → 1.3.13+)
Suggests OpenCode-side change in provider handling or tool-call flow formatting

Affect how third-party providers format tool calls

Only impact non-official provider paths

No provider-specific breakage for the same model capabilities

Actual behavior
